title: ‘Brilliant work’ – BBC pundit loved what Liverpool player did just before Alexander Isak goal
description: Alexander Isak fired Liverpool into the lead against Bournemouth this afternoon shortly before the hour mark, taking him to four goals for the season already and matching his tally from the whole of 2...
fullText:
Alexander Isak fired Liverpool into the lead against Bournemouth this afternoon shortly before the hour mark, taking him to four goals for the season already and matching his tally from the whole of 2025/26.

The first half had been a frustrating one for the Reds at the Vitality Stadium, with Andoni Iraola's side indebted to Alisson Becker for a brilliant reaction save from Evanilson to prevent his team from going behind.

The visitors didn't make the most auspicious of starts to the second half, either, but it was they who drew first blood on the south coast.

In the 57th minute, Cody Gakpo powered past Adrien Truffert on the right flank and delivered a cross into the penalty area that Florian Wirtz attempted to flick on. The ball fell to Isak, who anticipated the chance and promptly dispatched it past Djordje Petrovic.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, Rob Green was keen to give the Dutchman due credit for his role in the goal, saying: "Isak takes the plaudits from the Liverpool fans but it's Cody Gakpo down the right who does brilliant work and shrugs off two challenges.

"He finds the cross from under his feet and Antonio Silva, who's been brilliant, ducks the way out of the ball and I'm not sure why. That was the opportunity that Isak has been waiting for. No mistake from that."

(Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

All four of Isak's goals so far this season have been set up by Gakpo, whose contribution for the opener against Bournemouth was rightly praised by Green.

The persistence of Liverpool's number 18 in getting past Truffert and delivering the cross was exactly what Iraola would've loved to see, and it shows just why the Anfield hierarchy were right not to sell him to Manchester City in the final days of the summer transfer window.

The Dutchman was widely criticised by fans and pundits last season, when he played nowhere near his best, but he's been one of our best players in the opening month of this campaign.

The link-up between him and Isak has been increasingly productive, and it's a double act which could go a long way towards the Reds realising their ambitions for the 2026/27 season.

Both players deserve immense credit for how they've begun the campaign under Iraola.

title: Wrexham's boost & Alexander in ideal place - Aaron McLean's EFL takeaways
description: BBC Final Score pundit Aaron McLean looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including Wrexham, QPR and Bradford City.
fullText:
Former Peterborough United and Hull City striker - and Final Score pundit - Aaron McLean gives his five takeaways following Saturday's action in the Championship, League One and League Two.

Wrexham ended Southampton's five-match unbeaten run by winning 2-1 to claim their first home win of the season. Expectations remain high in north Wales, such is the public profile of the club and the investment into the squad but they have been an inconsistent prospect so far this campaign.

McLean: "Do I think Wrexham are a candidate for automatic promotion? Probably not, but that win against Southampton will give them huge confidence.

"That was only their second win of the season and they have probably come under pressure for the first time. Last season they were outstanding and, personally I think overachieved and the level of expectation has risen as a result but the team has not quite lived up to it.

"To beat Southampton, as one of the in-form teams in the division, will do them and Phil Parkinson no end of good.

"They need to be more clinical. You look at West Ham – 22 goals; Middlesbrough – 16 goals. You look at the top end of the pitch and they have the players who can find ways to kill games off.

"Wrexham have drawn four games because they have not been able to kill games off but, if they are in the shake-up, I would not bet against their owners in January saying, 'right, let's go and get the missing piece of the puzzle'."

Wrexham earn last-gasp victory over Southampton

Given Preston's predicament towards the foot of the Championship, QPR may well feel their 2-2 draw was two points dropped but they fought back from 2-0 down and Dennis Cirkin's red card in the 15th minute to claim a draw at Loftus Road. Julien Stephan's R's are fifth in the Championship table and remain firmly in the promotion mix.

McLean: "I have been so impressed with QPR. I think they have been outstanding and they can genuinely stay around the play-off places.

"Glen Kamara in the middle of the park is an outstanding player who I think could play in the Premier League. Their recruitment has been first class.

"With the squad they have got, I really like the look of them this season. For a few years they have probably spent money in the wrong places but they have addressed that and can look forward to having a really competitive season.

"Julien Stephan has done a hugely impressive job – the 7-1 defeat to Coventry [at the start of last season] has been the making of them – and I am really looking forward to seeing them over the rest of the season."

QPR score last-minute equaliser against Preston

Bradford City's 58-year wait for a win over Luton Town has enabled them to usurp Sheffield Wednesday at the top of League One. The Bantams have only scored seven goals in seven games but have conceded just four - the joint-best defensive record in the EFL. Predictably, given his history at Deepdale as a player, Graham Alexander has been linked with the vacancy at Preston North End.

McLean: "Bradford are a massive club, you only have to listen to the noise they make at Valley Parade and the support they get and Graham Alexander is an outstanding manager who is at the right club for him to continue progressing.

"This season, their bouncebackability has stood out. They won their first two games, then after back-to-back defeats you are looking at them and thinking, 'oh was it just a good start' but then they go and win three in a row, so even in adversity they can bounce back and respond in the right way.

"Is their lack of goals sustainable for a promotion challenge? No, probably not but, at the moment, it hasn't needed to be because they have been so good defensively and so hard to beat.

"And that's from front to back and when they do get their noses in front, they know how to see games out.

"I expect their conversion rate to improve and Bobby Pointon is a fantastic young striker who I have tipped to be one of the best strikers in the division over the next few seasons."

Bromley ended Huddersfield Town's unbeaten start to the season with a 2-1 victory at the Copperjax Community Stadium - their first since the opening day of the 2026-27 season. It has been a challenging first few weeks for the club in the third tier for the first time in their history, losing three games in a row and conceding 14 goals in the process but Andy Woodman's squad have shown their resilience and quality to come through that period.

McLean: "For Bromley, it is sometimes easy to lose sight of where they have come from, how quickly they have got here, and the jump that exists between League Two and the top end of League One. It is really, really tough for newly-promoted teams and it is going to take time to adapt.

"To come out winners against Huddersfield who were the form team in the division will do them the world of good.

"It shows they have the character and the belief in the dressing room that even on the back of a run of defeats they can go again, and compete and get positive results against teams of the size of Huddersfield.

"Andy Woodman will be absolutely delighted. For a club of Bromley's size and where they have been, consolidation in League One will surely be the goal this season and these three points will go a long way to helping achieve that."

Since dropping down to League Two four years ago, Gillingham have never finished higher than 12th, a poor return for a club of their size and reputation. But their eye-catching 3-0 win over Bristol Rovers means they are now the form side in the division with three wins and three draws over their past six and have moved up to fourth with signs pointing towards something stirring within Gareth Ainsworth's squad.

McLean: "I spoke to Gareth Ainsworth in the summer and he admitted he got it wrong last season. They perhaps overachieved a bit at the start and that created a false impression of where they were as a squad.

"Gareth has ripped up the script a bit and they have looked really really positive and are playing their way into form.

"He is huge on the psychological aspect of management and players 'emptying the tank' and to play for Gareth Ainsworth you have to buy into that.

"When you look at their performances and the way they are achieving these results it looks like another squad of players who have bought into his ideas.

"You look at his Wycombe sides, you don't have to be the biggest club in the division as long as everyone is pulling in the right direction then you can be successful."

Aaron McLean was speaking to BBC Sport England's James Piercy

title: A weight off Igor Thiago's shoulders - Brentford v Chelsea ratings
description: Brentford climb to third in the Premier League with a 2-0 victory over Chelsea - here are BBC Sport's player ratings.
fullText:
Brentford climbed to third in the Premier League with an impressive 3-0 victory over Chelsea.

Goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and substitute Fabio Carvalho secured the three points as Chelsea's winless league run extended to three matches.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Caoimhin Kelleher: An accomplished display, although he was never required to make any outstanding saves. 6

Michael Kayode: Played a couple of sloppy passes and rarely ventured forward. 6

Kristoffer Ajer: A sizeable presence at the back despite coming under significant pressure from crosses in open play and from set-pieces. 7

Jannik Schuster: The young defender excelled in his own box but looked nervous in possession on a few occasions, including an overhit backpass that could have led to an own goal. He then set up the winner. 7

Keane Lewis-Potter: A poor clearance led to a Neto chance in the 10th minute, but he was impressive on the counter-attack. That perhaps owed something to his experience of learning the left-back role after previously playing as an attacker. 6

Yehor Yarmoliuk: On his 100th appearance, he threatened with a powerful long-range effort in the 37th minute and created Brentford's best chance shortly after half-time. 7

Vitaly Janelt: Did just enough to halt a Cole Palmer dribble early on, although he risked conceding a penalty. He provided a physical presence in midfield, with a potential Germany debut on the horizon under new manager Jurgen Klopp. 7

Mikkel Damsgaard: The Dane was not at his usual level from set-pieces or with his shooting from distance until he delivered an incredible whipped corner that led to the opening goal. 6

Kevin Schade: The in-form forward produced several pressure-relieving dribbles and had a shot blocked in the first half. Played a part in the final two goals. 7

Igor Thiago: The Brazil international was on a four-game goalless run before kick-off and worked hard but struggled in front of goal. He eventually delivered with a late strike to seal victory and his celebration looked like a weight then lifted off his shoulders, along with his Brentford shirt. 7

Jaidon Anthony: After a quiet first half, he missed his side's best chance early in the second half but responded well to score the opener. 7

Mamadou Sangare (on 72, Yarmoliuk): Did his combative duties well. 7

Aaron Hickey (on 72, Kayode): A steady presence. 6

El Hadji Malick Diouf (on 81, Lewis-Potter): N/A

Dango Ouattara (on 81, Anthony): N/A

Fabio Carvalho (on 87, Damsgaard): Ghosted in nicely to add a goal late on in a very short spell on the pitch. 7

Subs not used: Ballcombe, Henry, Wilson, Frederick

Emiliano Martinez: The Argentine did not face any clear chances or difficult set-pieces in the first half. There was little he could do about Brentford's opener. 6

Wesley Fofana: The Frenchman was a physical presence at the back and dealt well enough with Brentford's long balls but was taken off for Josh Acheampong in the 72nd minute. 6

Maxence Lacroix: He coped well with Igor Thiago for most of the match, winning the majority of his duels, but he gave the ball away for Brentford's second goal and he missed a clear chance in the dying moments. 4

Levi Colwill: A quiet match by his high standards after being left out of the England squad. 6

Pedro Neto: His well-struck effort was saved in the 10th minute. He was lively throughout, linking up well in attack and stretching Brentford with his pace. 6

Jordan Henderson: There were no signs of rust. After receiving some early boos, he settled into the game and looked a vocal leader on the pitch. He also put some good corners into the box. 7

Valentin Barco: On his first Premier League start, the Argentine impressed defensively and was more ambitious with his passing than Henderson. 6

Pep Chavarria: Produced some dangerous crosses and was tidy in possession. A largely positive display despite one piece of naive defending in the first half that led to a free-kick. 7

Cole Palmer: Undoubtedly Chelsea's best player on the night, with much of their attacking play going through him. However, he was unable to produce the decisive moment he craved, with a free-kick comfortably saved and few other clear opportunities. He also worked hard defensively. 7

Danny Welbeck: On his first Premier League start for Chelsea, the 35-year-old created a chance for Neto but did not do enough to compensate for the absence of injured striker Joao Pedro. His 72nd minute withdrawal said a lot. 5

Morgan Rogers: Had a dangerous effort blocked in the penalty area just before half-time. The club-record £117m signing could also have done more to win the header at the back post for Brentford's opener. He ended the match playing up front as a striker. 5

Josh Acheampong (on 72, Fofana): It was unclear why Acheampong came on when he did and, as a young defender, didn't make much impact in these circumstances. 6

Geovany Quenda (on 72, Welbeck): Impressively got on the ball often and tried to make something happen for Chelsea but without any results. 6

Estevao Willian (on 87, Neto): N/A

Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli (on 87, Barco): N/A

Subs not used: Penders, Gusto, Hato, Lavia, Gittens

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

title: Trump says he's banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House
description:
— President Donald Trump said Friday that he was banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House due to what he called unfavorable coverage, and threatened that more such media prohibitions could be coming — offering his administration's latest test of constitutional First Amendment protections guaranteeing the freedom of the press.
Trump has long bristled at news coverage he maintains casts him in a negative light, and has a history of filing lawsuits against news organizations, while lashing out at individual reporters in person or over social media.
The move follows the president's decision, in February 2025, to keep Associated Press journalists out of the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events too small for a full press corps, in retaliation for the news outlet's decision not to follow his lead in changing the Gulf of Mexico's name.
The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Since returning to office, however, Trump has pursued other legal action against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Friday that he was banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House due to what he called unfavorable coverage, and threatened that more such media prohibitions could be coming — offering his administration's latest test of constitutional First Amendment protections guaranteeing the freedom of the press.

Trump has long bristled at news coverage he maintains casts him in a negative light, and has a history of filing lawsuits against news organizations, while lashing out at individual reporters in person or over social media.

The move follows the president's decision, in February 2025, to keep Associated Press journalists out of the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events too small for a full press corps, in retaliation for the news outlet's decision not to follow his lead in changing the Gulf of Mexico's name.

The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Since returning to office, however, Trump has pursued other legal action against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC.

Trump seeking to block White House access for CNN is especially notably, however, as it could upend the traditional five-network television pool that travels with the president and tracks his every move — meant to provide independent coverage of his actions and interactions for the Americans who elected him and the world.

In the social media announcement, Trump did not provide details on how the ban would be implemented.

It came moments before Trump spoke to reporters in the Oval Office as part of a health care event. He later planned to take the press pool to his golf club in Virginia for a meeting and dinner sponsored by his Super PAC before spending the weekend at Camp David — one of the few places reporters don't follow him.

The president wrote on his social media site that effective immediately, "I am banning" CNN, MSNOW and Politico "from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!"

"Media Outlets shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America," Trump wrote. "Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow."

title: How Iraola is moving Liverpool on from the Slot era
description: BBC Sport looks at how new manager Andoni Iraola is moving Liverpool on from the Arne Slot era after their disappointing form last season.
fullText:
Only 12 months ago Liverpool had won each of their first five Premier League games and were seemingly on their way to defending their crown under Arne Slot.

That run started with victory over a Bournemouth side led by Andoni Iraola on the opening night of the season.

Surely no one thought then that, come the end of the campaign, Iraola would be replacing Slot at Anfield.

Such is the volatility of football, it is too early to pass judgement on Iraola - even if his Liverpool side are already six points worse off than they were at this stage last season.

Under the 44-year-old, Liverpool are still unbeaten and this weekend Iraola returns to the place he called home for three years.

It will certainly be an odd feeling when he enters the smaller away changing room at Bournemouth - the Cherries have had to renovate it to comply with Europa League regulations, so at least it will be a slightly more pleasant experience than it would have been previously.

Iraola has swapped the seaside on the south coast for the beach town of Formby, where former Liverpool managers Jurgen Klopp and Brendan Rodgers also resided. By all accounts, he is settling in well. He has been spotted in the city centre on a few occasions and, as a keen cyclist, has enjoyed the coastal routes.

But Iraola is most at home on the training ground. He is very much a 'six days a week' coach, according to those at Liverpool, and such is his passion for coaching that he is often the first on the training pitch, marking the cones out for sessions.

"It's really intense. There's a lot of hard work and no sort of light days. Everyone's putting in 100%," said forward Lewis Koumas.

Those at Liverpool are firmly of the belief that everyone associated with the club was glad to get last season out of the way and that even if Slot had remained as head coach, things were always going to feel better.

At Liverpool's AXA Training Centre in Kirkby, Iraola rarely uses his own office and is often found in the coaches room where his assistants in Tommy Elphick, Shaun Cooper and Pablo de la Torre are based, and he has a relatively low-key presence in and around the building, compared to previous managers.

De la Torre, who moved with Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth in 2023, is seen as a key pillar in ensuring that the players are all up to the physical standard that Iraola wants.

In terms of actual changes inside the club they are not as big as people may think from the outside, given the structured nature of the head coach role.

Iraola's appointment was based on his fine work at Bournemouth but he is very much learning on the job when it comes to dealing with Liverpool's congested schedule.

There is a willingness to listen to other departments like the medical and fitness teams at Kirkby as the Reds seek to manage a squad that will play at least 49 games this season - a number that could climb into the 60s depending on Liverpool's cup runs.

When it comes to the training schedule, Iraola tends to adapt it in line with the kick-off time for the following fixture, with late afternoon and early evening sessions increasingly common. Under Slot, Liverpool tended to train at a similar time each day.

There have also been conversations with the academy and Rob Page, who coaches Liverpool Under-21s.

"We have an understanding of how the first team play and key principles, like how we press, how he [Iraola] wants his number 10 to press, how he wants his number eight to press, how he wants his centre-backs to press - we mirror that absolutely," said Page.

Earlier this week, Dominik Szoboszlai explained how Liverpool play with a number six, a number eight and a number 10 - and, despite calls for a defensive midfielder from fans during the transfer window, Iraola's system can work if everyone improves collectively.

Iraola's preference is to name the team on the morning of the game and he saves the post-match debrief with his players for the day after the match.

There is a sense of pragmatism with his media interactions, too, after a situation where his comments to LFC TV following a pre-season friendly against Monaco were widely reported.

Iraola conceded Liverpool had run out of steam after 30 minutes and did not have the energy levels at the time to play with the intensity that he wants. It wasn't meant to be a dig at his players - rather an admittance that they were working on building that intensity up.

But there is a realisation that at a club like Liverpool, every word you say can end up shared across social media and taken in a different way than you meant. That said, Iraola comes across as calm in his news conferences and open to discussion.

It is very much a case of Iraola adapting to the club as much as the other way round.

One of the main reasons they went for Iraola was his ability to develop young talent and the average age of Liverpool's players in the Premier League this season is 25.3 - only five teams have a lower average.

Youngsters like Rio Ngumoha, 18, Trey Nyoni, 19, and Koumas, 20, all started against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup and all three will play bigger roles this season than last.

Intensity is a buzzword under Iraola and that is a non-negotiable but he is already aware that, with such a brutal schedule, Liverpool will need to find ways to adapt and occasionally win games with a set-piece or an individual moment of brilliance.

Going into this weekend, they have made the most sprints in the Premier League but looked flat against Fulham last weekend in a goalless draw, less than 72 hours after beating Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Sunday's game against Bournemouth will be a fourth in 12 days and, after the international break, Liverpool have a spell of four games in 10 days. Between 11 October and 7 November, they will play nine times.

Iraola would no doubt have had a smile seeing Bournemouth win on their Europa League bow against Real Sociedad on Thursday, in the Basque region where he grew up.

Perhaps he will have a moment on the flight down from Liverpool on Saturday to think about how far he has come.

Liverpool haven't exactly had a dream start under Iraola but they are yet to lose. Becoming a team that is hard to beat is undoubtedly a step in the right direction after 12 league losses last term, but as vice-captain Alisson said last week, draws aren't good enough for Liverpool.

And Iraola, who is unbeaten in the Premier League since January across his two clubs, knows that a win on familiar territory on Sunday would be the perfect way to head into the international break.

title: BBC to broadcast World Rally Championship from 2027
description: The BBC will broadcast the FIA World Rally Championship across the UK from 2027-29.
fullText:
The BBC will broadcast the FIA World Rally Championship across the UK from 2027-29.

The new deal includes coverage of all 14 WRC rounds each season, with five live stages plus the power stage from each rally, 14 one-hour highlights programmes, digital clips and additional content across BBC platforms.

Rally Scotland will receive extensive live coverage across all four days of competition, giving audiences in the UK live, free-to-air access to the country's first WRC round since 2019.

Hugh Chambers, CEO of Motorsport UK, the organisation behind Rally Scotland, said: "The BBC agreement gives Rally Scotland and the wider WRC a national platform from 2027, helping us reach long-standing fans and bring new audiences into the sport."

Welshman Elfyn Evans leads the 2026 championship with one round of the season remaining, the Rally Italia Sardegna from 1 October to 4 October.

title: Sutton's predictions v legendary guitarist Johnny Marr
description: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on legendary guitarist and Man City fan Johnny Marr, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.
fullText:
The pressure is growing on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, but can his side sign off for the three-week international break by beating Fulham on Sunday?

"For teams who have had a bad start to the season, United being one of them, it could be a horrible few weeks," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"Any negativity is going to just fester, really. There will be speculation about his future, along with all the talk about whether this is a good time to replace your manager.

"United are not the only team to have made a bad start, but there is a lot to ponder on for them at the moment. It makes this weekend even more important."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.

For week four, he takes on legendary guitarist and Manchester City fan, Johnny Marr.

Marr's new album, The Age Of Everything, is out on 2 October.

Do you agree with their scores? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competitions.

Marr has enjoyed City's 100% start to the new Premier League season, with Sunday's win at Old Trafford continuing their impressive start under new boss Enzo Maresca.

"I think that derby will be remembered by City fans for a long time," Marr told BBC Sport.

"We all feared the worst when Phil Foden was sent off so early, because you don't know what could happen. It should have been a yellow card for him and Bruno Fernandes anyway.

"It's all a bit of a learning curve for the fans and the club with a new manager and so many new players, so to see how the team dug in and won was so great for City fans.

"No-one expected Maresca to win his first four games... but then again, why not? He's shown that he's his own man with his own philosophy. I like him."

Chris Sutton and Johnny Marr were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Gtech Community Stadium, 20:00 BST

Chelsea are free-scoring and their front-line is so dynamic - but they are leaking goals left, right and centre and they are a bit of a rabble at the back.

I do think Chelsea will stop conceding eventually, but finding the right balance between defence and attack is Xabi Alonso's big problem at the moment because it is far too easy to create chances against his side.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews has got that balance in his team. They are very dangerous on the counter-attack, so you have to think they will hurt Chelsea too.

This fixture finished in a 2-2 draw in September last year, and I can see it going the same way this time.

Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, 12:30

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi has this reputation of being a great coach, and we saw what a good job he did at Brighton.

But we have not seen any improvement from Spurs yet, despite the big money they have spent, and he is surely going to come under pressure soon if their poor results continue.

They are not the only ones to revamp their squad but if you listen to De Zerbi, after about five years they might come good.

He keeps saying they need time, but he has had long enough for their results to be much better already. Other clubs, like Hull and Ipswich, have brought plenty of players in and are doing well enough - so why aren't Spurs?

I think De Zerbi has to come under scrutiny, but it is different with Unai Emery at Aston Villa.

They are also without a league win, but they look more likely to score goals, as they showed against Coventry in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

I am expecting Villa to improve the same way they did after not winning any of their first five games last season, and I can see them edging this.

Do I give Spurs their first league goal of the season? Yes, but only one. They are due a deflection, or Villa will score an own goal.

Something will go for them, but not the result.

There might be a bit of an edge to this one after Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler had a pop at Arsenal over their time-wasting when they beat the Seagulls near the end of last season.

I love the way Brighton play and I was at Old Trafford to watch their comeback to beat Manchester United in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

It doesn't seem to matter who they are missing from their team, Brighton are just bold as brass with the way they press and get men forward.

Luka Vuskovic, who they got from Spurs for £46m in the summer, is only 19 but he strolled through the game against United. What a player he looks.

The issue I have with Brighton in this game, however, is that Arsenal are not Manchester United. They are a cut above that.

Arsenal are the real deal and I don't see any weaknesses in their team, as their impressive win at Sunderland underlined. They are brave going forward, but they are also street-wise defensively and can see out a game when they have to, time-wasting or not.

They have that steel about them but I also think they could expose Brighton if Hurzeler's side go toe-to-toe with them, which is what I am expecting.

I nearly went for an Ipswich draw last week but changed my mind and went for Crystal Palace to win.

That meant I'd predicted Ipswich would lose their first four league games and they are joint-bottom of the table based on my predictions (see bottom of page).

Gary O'Neil's side have obviously done much better than that in reality - I know Palace went down to 10 men last week but, even so, well done to the Tractor Boys for finding a way to win that game.

Fair play to them, I like the ambition the club's owners have shown in the transfer market, and I really like the way O'Neil sets his team up. They are not just there to sit in in games, and they have got their reward.

I still fancy Everton to win this, though. They have made a great start to the season to stay unbeaten so far and, under David Moyes, they are a battle-hardened, resolute and well-organised outfit.

As a former Norwich striker I often get accused of being biased against Ipswich, but I am not being overly negative about them here.

I just see it being a tough afternoon for them, without getting a goal, and then a long trip home for Ipswich fans on the A14 - hopefully they don't close any of the major roads on Saturday so it is not an even more miserable journey back for them.

I can see this being a frustrating afternoon for Newcastle because they are going to come up against a Hull team who are brilliant at defending the box but are also brave with the way they throw people forward.

They are a threat from set-plays too but they have got the bit between their teeth and their whole attitude seems to be 'attack the Premier League' after getting promoted, which I really admire.

Along with Ipswich, Hull are the only other team I've predicted to lose all their games so far.

I am going to tip them not to lose this time... so you know what is probably going to happen. Apologies in advance to Tigers fans, because this happened with me and Sunderland last season.

Coventry were served up a couple of shockers by getting Arsenal and Manchester City as their first two away fixtures and this trip is far from easy for them either.

In fact this is another stinker of a game for Sky Blues boss Frank Lampard, because they are still struggling while Oliver Glasner seems to be getting Nottingham Forest going after a slow burner of a start.

There is a strong chance that Coventry's confidence has been sapped already so Lampard will be trying to rally the troops and give his players some belief that they can compete at this level.

That is going to be really difficult because they must be looking at the results of the other promoted teams and not just thinking 'where is a win coming from for us?' - but also 'where is a point coming from?', and 'where is a goal coming from?' too.

I don't think they will get any of those things this week, because Forest are looking pretty solid.

Well done to Forest striker Liam Delap by the way, who got his first goal for them in last week's win at Aston Villa.

He had a tough time at Chelsea, and I know what that is like, so it is great to see him off the mark for his new club.

My value went down by almost 50% when I left Stamford Bridge - from £10m to £6m - so what has gone on there?

Seriously, though, sometimes you need a change of scene to find your form again and Delap must be feeling a bit freer now he has his first Forest goal.

I am not convinced by Liverpool at all after covering them for Radio 5 Live last week - I thought Fulham were the better side in their 0-0 draw at Anfield.

Andoni Iraola's side did not flow in the final third, certainly not in the way his Bournemouth team did last season.

I don't think the Reds players are quite in sync with what Iraola is asking them to do in terms of their press either, and Fulham played through them with ease at times.

Marco Rose is an attacking manager so if Liverpool don't buck their ideas up then Bournemouth are going to do the same, and Iraola could end up losing on his return to his former club.

The one thing in Iraola's favour is that Bournemouth seem to be finding a way to draw games that they should win, so that is the result I am going with even though though I quite fancy the Cherries to take all three points.

I think I am in love with Leeds boss Daniel Farke. What a guy.

We were talking about him on the Monday Night Club before Leeds walloped Newcastle and only idiots question whether he is the right man to move the club forward now.

To see them beat Newcastle, and how emphatically they did it, was massive and more proof of their progress.

In contrast, Crystal Palace are almost on the precipice after their shaky start under new manager Pierre Sage, and I just don't see the Eagles getting anything here.

Leeds are so well organised at the back with new goalkeeper James Trafford, who is an upgrade on last season, and and a new centre-half I like too, in Tarik Muharemovic.

Apart from me, no-one else could say Muharemovic's name on the Monday Night Club, not even the posh Rory Smith, which I quite enjoyed.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is flying up front, as well. He is fit, motivated and a real handful, which is another reason I can't see past a Leeds victory.

Sunderland are a really good team and, on their day, they are more than a match for anyone.

The Black Cats are strong and robust, and when they get after teams and press you then they are phenomenal.

All of that makes me think this is a really hard game for Manchester City.

Their derby victory was a brilliant win and Maresca's biggest result as their manager so far, with the way they did it.

Iliman Ndiaye showed what a good signing he is when he came on for Rayan Cherki in the second half at Old Trafford, in terms of offering a different profile.

Cherki's more of an inside forward, as a number 10 or playing narrow, and he's a guy where you think you couldn't get the ball off him in a telephone box.

Ndiaye, though, will do more work going back and is also more of a ball carrier, so he was exactly what City needed when they went a man down.

United can feel hard done by because City's winner should have been disallowed, but City were the better team with 10 men.

This will be a very different task for Maresca's men, with the emphasis on them breaking down the Black Cats, but I don't feel it will just be one-way traffic.

I still think City will find a way though, and they need to for the sake of the title race. They already seem to be the only team capable of keeping pace with Arsenal.

Johnny on former boss Pep Guardiola, who stepped down in the summer, and his favourite City players: No-one expected Pep to stay for 10 years so it made him leaving OK to accept, and good luck to him. Aside from the success he brought to the club, City fans loved him because he totally loved Manchester.

Dennis Tueart was my favourite player when I was a kid and I think he could have played in this current era. We've had amazing players in the last 12 or so years so how do you pick, but my favourites would be Vincent Kompany, Sergio Aguero and David Silva, with the top place going to Kevin De Bruyne. I'd say he's the best player I've seen in a City shirt.

Watching Fulham draw at Anfield last weekend changed my view on them.

I had not seen Alvaro Arbeloa's side over 90 minutes before and, while their other results were poor, this time they were excellent.

They cut through Liverpool and had some nice patterns of play, but also defended well too. Arbeloa said afterwards that they played with more balance and I think that is a good way to describe their display.

Then I went to Manchester United's defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, and their performance was very poor.

Carrick really needs a response with a win here to take into the international break but how can I give United a chance, after the way the Seagulls absolutely dismantled them?

Three times in the past four seasons, United have gone to Craven Cottage and nicked the win late on, but I can't make a case for that happening.

As well as having problems up front, United are struggling defensively and I can see Fulham creating plenty of opportunities against them too.

Chris and his guest, Dorking Wanderers boss Marc White, both got four correct results with no exact scores from the 10 games in week four, giving them 40 points each.

AI did better, thanks to an exact score for Brentford's 2-2 draw with Bournemouth which, along with two other correct results, gave it a total of 60 points.

But it was the collective efforts of the BBC readers who took the weekly win - their first of the season - that also sees them move from bottom to level on points with Chris at the top of the predictions table.

They also got one exact score - Arsenal's 2-0 win at Sunderland - but also managed four correct results, giving them a total of 40 points.

It was a tough week for predictions, with only two games where everyone picked the right outcome - that victory for the Gunners, and Brighton's win at Coventry.

There were five games where none of our predictors guessed the result - Nottingham Forest's win at Aston Villa, Hull's draw at Chelsea, Ipswich's win at Crystal Palace, Fulham's draw at Liverpool and Leeds' win over Newcastle.

The biggest shock of the week came at Anfield. From more than 33,000 predictions, just under 30,000 (91%) of you went for a Liverpool win, while fewer than 2,000 of you went for any sort of draw and only 390 of you got the correct 0-0 scoreline.

title: The big questions for Tuchel's first England squad since World Cup
description: Before Thomas Tuchel names his first squad since the World Cup on Friday, BBC Sport looks at the big questions facing the England boss.
fullText:
Sixty-five days after England's semi-final defeat by Argentina, Thomas Tuchel will name his first squad since the World Cup on Friday.

While the tournament ultimately ended with a spectacular 6-4 win over France in the bronze-medal match, the Three Lions left the United States with a long list of what ifs.

Now, with four games in the space of 11 days coming up during the extended international break, fans will get a glimpse of what Tuchel's next England side might look like.

Could players like Trent Alexander-Arnold be recalled? Will others like Alex Scott make their debut? And how might we expect them to play?

BBC Sport senior football correspondent Sami Mokbel, journalist Jess Anderson and BBC Radio 5 Live's John Murray go through the big questions facing Tuchel.

Sami Mokbel: Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Hall are among the players to have been named in England manager Thomas Tuchel's provisional squad for the forthcoming Nations League internationals, though it remains to be seen whether they make the final cut.

Liverpool winger Ngumoha was part of a contingent of young players that flew with the England senior squad for their pre-World Cup training camp in Palm Beach.

He was unexpectedly handed his debut in the warm-up game against New Zealand, impressing in a second-half cameo.

But the 18-year-old is yet to be picked in a full senior England squad - although he is in with a chance of being selected by Tuchel for the forthcoming games against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia.

Hall's World Cup omission raised eyebrows given England entered the tournament without a natural left-back.

Before naming his full squad on Friday, Tuchel is required to submit a preliminary squad of players from which he will name his final party.

It is understood Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly and Everton pair Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Jarrad Branthwaite are also among the names selected in Tuchel's extended list.

Attacking duo Cole Palmer and Phil Foden are on there too, after being two of the biggest omissions from Tuchel's squad for the World Cup.

That decision was deemed a mistake from certain circles, given they are two of English football's most creative players.

Meanwhile, Tuchel is expected to omit Jordan Henderson, Dean Henderson and John Stones because of injury.

Tuchel regrets not eating Azteca turf after win over Mexico

FA to canvass England players in World Cup review

Jess Anderson: One of the most talked-about issues surrounding England is who they turn to in the absence of captain and star striker Harry Kane. At the World Cup, Tuchel simply did not turn to anyone. Kane started all seven of England's matches up to the semi-final and was substituted only twice - both times late on with the game already won.

Kane was rested for the bronze-medal match, with Ivan Toney the preferred option, although the Al-Ahli striker did not score in the 6-4 win over France. Toney will not be an option this international break as he has since been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm and is due to appear in court later this month.

Ollie Watkins' shock summer move to Saudi Arabia puts his England future into question, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the man in form with four goals in four games for Leeds United.

This could be the moment for Tuchel to start to further integrate Liam Delap, who is improving at new club Nottingham Forest and has yet to make a senior England appearance. He scored his first goal for Forest in last weekend's win at Aston Villa.

John Murray: In the immediate aftermath of the semi-final in Atlanta, Tuchel and the players spoke of being too passive. At the squad announcement it will be interesting to hear what conclusions Tuchel has reached on why that was the case, and how they came to surrender the initiative to Argentina from 1-0 up with just over half an hour to play.

Head of the queue for a recall is Cole Palmer, who seems to have recaptured the form he was missing last season, which resulted in his omission from the World Cup squad.

What England fans will want to see against Spain at Wembley, is Palmer and his like taking the initiative and imposing themselves on their opponents in a way that was so lacking in the latter stages against Argentina in July.

John Murray: Happy or not, that's what they've got - but this has to be better than another group of qualifiers such as the one they had for the World Cup, against teams way below them in the world rankings.

In those matches last autumn England played some of the best football they have so far produced under Tuchel.

But, while that helped establish patterns of play and build confidence, you never really know until you face the best. That clearly will be the case from the outset in the Nations League, with this opening match against the new world champions.

These matches will also provide preparation for the next Euros in 2028 when, assuming they qualify, England will be playing opponents like this at Wembley. And, lest you forget, this tournament does provide an opportunity to win a trophy which would be the best possible way for Tuchel and his team to step on from their third place at the World Cup.

Sami Mokbel: This will be a key theme to watch over the next three weeks. The spirit was high in the England camp during the World Cup - as evidenced by their brilliant victory against Mexico in the last 16 with 10 men.

But the devastating semi-final defeat by Argentina, and questions over England's approach as a 1-0 lead became a 2-1 loss late on, led to some form of an inquest in the England camp into what was to blame.

Away from the height of those emotions in July, the Football Association is completing a review into England's World Cup campaign. The FA has been keen to stress that this assessment is a standard process, rather than an indication of wider concern or alarm about England's third-place finish.

Indeed, key figures at the FA view the tournament in which England achieved their best finish since 1966 as a success, and the organisation has already backed Tuchel before the Euro 2028 qualifying campaign.

Tuchel and members of his backroom team gave their contributions to the review at St George's Park in late August. England players' opinions are also being gathered before a report is presented to senior bosses at the FA.

The ongoing review will also look into the impact of the team's permanent Kansas City base during the tournament. After every game, they returned to Kansas City - and the effects of the travelling will be analysed.

The content of the review won't be made public, but the next three weeks will give an indication of whether the camp is still as together as that night at the Azteca.

title: Why EFL matches get postponed for international call-ups
description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why some League One and League two matches get postponed due to international call-ups.
fullText:
Matches in League One and League Two can be postponed during international breaks due to players being selected for international matches.

The English Football League (EFL) allows clubs to postpone fixtures should they receive a sufficient number of call-ups.

At least three of players have to be selected for their country's senior, under-21, under-20 or under-19 sides in order to request a postponement.

Players who are named on international standby lists or long lists will not count towards the three players at the time of announcement.

International age group players only qualify if they have been named in the starting XI, or been a named substitute making an appearance prior to the 75th minute, in either:

50% of a club's first-team matches

four of the last five first-team matches

If a player is signed by a club in either late August or during the January transfer window and they then get called up, a pro rata basis is used to determine if that player is available.

A team is also allowed to request a postponement if both the first and second choice goalkeepers are called up too.

Players signed on loan also count.

As per Fifa's guidelines, players selected must be released by their clubs by the Monday morning ahead of the first international fixtures of that window.

For home clubs wishing to request a postponement, they must do so at least five days prior to the game they wish to postpone.

Away teams must submit a request seven days in advance.

title: How an Aston Villa fringe player became Europe's most prolific scorer
description: No player in Europe's top five leagues has scored more goals than Donyell Malen since his Roma debut in January - BBC Sport examines his transformation.
fullText:
Just eight months ago, Donyell Malen was struggling to make a significant impact at Aston Villa.

Today, no player in Europe's top five leagues has scored more goals since his Roma debut on 18 January.

The Netherlands international has enjoyed a remarkable turnaround since joining Roma, transforming from a player who struggled to establish himself in the Premier League into one of the continent's most productive forwards.

Since his Roma debut, Malen has scored 20 goals, more than Harry Kane (16), Lamine Yamal (15) and anyone else in the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 during the same period.

He also leads the way for combined goals and assists with 22, ahead of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (20), Barcelona's teenage sensation Lamine Yamal (19) and Bayern striker Kane (18).

No player across Europe's top five leagues has made a greater contribution in front of goal.

The contrast with his time at Villa could hardly be greater.

In 46 appearances for the Premier League club, the 27-year-old scored 10 goals and registered two assists. Since joining Roma, he has scored 21 goals and provided three assists in just 25 matches.

His scoring rate has improved from one goal every 149.8 minutes at Villa to one every 96.7 minutes in Rome.

On the surface, the figures suggest two very different versions of the same player. But Roma's success with Malen may owe as much to how he is being used as to any change in confidence or form.

The Dutchman arrived in Italy with a proven goalscoring pedigree and the data suggests Roma have found a role that maximises his attacking instincts.

While confidence and form may have played a part, a change in position appears to be a major factor behind the resurgence.

At Villa, Malen was often used across the frontline and spent only 52% of his league minutes as a central striker. At Roma, 99% of his Serie A minutes have come through the middle under manager Gian Piero Gasperini, making him the focal point of the attack and placing him where he can do the most damage.

The stats are backed up by the eye test. After Roma's 1-1 Champions League draw with Fenerbahce last Thursday, when Malen set up his side's goal, French football journalist Julien Laurens told Match of the Day the Dutchman had become central to Gasperini's plans.

"He has been incredible since January," said Laurens.

"He has been really efficient, super clinical. Malen is at the heart of everything they do with the ball."

Malen is not the only former Premier League player to have flourished in Italy.

Former Manchester United midfielder Scott McTominay has thrived since swapping Old Trafford for Naples. Since joining Napoli in August 2024, only five players have scored more Serie A goals than the Scotland international's 22.

His impact has been such that Napoli supporters have even erected a street shrine in his honour.

Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund has also enjoyed an upturn in fortunes. His time in north west England divided opinion among supporters and pundits alike.

But since his Napoli debut, only Federico Dimarco, Lautaro Martinez and Malen have recorded more goal involvements than the Denmark international (19).

Their success highlights how a move to Serie A can provide players with the opportunity to thrive in a different environment and role.

For Malen, however, the transformation has been particularly dramatic.

Rather than changing Malen's game, Roma appear to have found a role that gets the best out of him. Used almost exclusively as a striker, the Dutchman has responded by producing the kind of form that first brought him to the attention of Europe's biggest clubs.

For a player whose Premier League spell failed to meet expectations, his resurgence in Italy's capital ranks among the most notable revivals in European football this year.

title: Why dealing with defeat is key for Lampard at Coventry
description: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Coventry boss Frank Lampard needs to manage himself as well as his players after their poor start to the season.
fullText:
Managing a newly promoted team in the Premier League is very demanding, as Frank Lampard is finding out at Coventry.

It's the highest level, not just for the technical ability of the players that your team faces but also the sheer physicality that these players possess, and it feels like the gap to the Championship is getting greater every season.

From my experience in the same situation, you have to be really smart in the way you approach each game and recognise the importance of preparation for each specific opponent, because your team has to be organised in possession, and definitely out of possession.

Teams in the Premier League counter-attack with greater efficiency so being solid behind your own attacking play is absolutely vital.

But the real advice I would give to managers in Frank's shoes is to manage yourself, and your own time, as well as your players.

I can tell you now that, whoever you are playing, if you get beaten - and especially beaten heavily like Coventry were by Brighton on Sunday - then it resonates with you. It's the same for every manager.

For Frank, whether it is losing at home to Hull or Brighton, or against Arsenal and Manchester City, then it will hurt.

But it is how he deals with those defeats that will decide what happens next.

Being the leader of a group of young men, you cannot look washed out and empty on a Monday morning after a heavy loss.

Yes, inside you will be hurting and your pride will be taking a bashing but everyone at the club will be waiting for your reaction, and will act accordingly.

Walking into the training ground in a dark mood and with your head around your backside just does not work, irrespective of what you are feeling inside.

I've been in that situation many times myself as a manager and what you have to do is puff your chest out and find a way of getting everyone back on track and working even harder with a set focus on the next game.

That's what all good leaders do. It is draining at times, but that is why managing your time and prioritising the issues that you can resolve is so important.

When I took Stoke up to the Premier League in 2008, I was learning on my feet.

We did not make a great start and I had to roll my sleeves up and get on with what I'd got in my squad, and really focus on getting results.

But away from that I was always forward thinking and I was quick at recognising what was needed to improve our chances of staying up.

When the window opened again in January, we were already in discussions with Tottenham for Matty Etherington, to supply us with crosses and chances from the wing.

We needed more goals too, so I took James Beattie from Sheffield United. They were a Championship side but that didn't matter because he had a record of scoring goals in the top flight.

We have heard so much about recruiting the right players in the right positions, and it is true today as it was in my day. Both lads played a significant role in keeping us up.

Coventry haven't scored a goal yet, and people might look in from the outside and feel the forward areas are an issue for them because the usual thinking is that the centre-forward has to lead the scoring charts, or a wide player or the number 10.

But the emphasis is on everyone to chip in and I would also reinforce one of the points I made in this column last season, about the importance of defending properly too.

On average, clean sheets earn you more points than scoring a goal, which is something I always stressed to my players. Nailing down the importance of both ends of the pitch is the narrative, whatever kind of run of results you are on, because games are won and lost there.

Coventry have made a poor start but what has happened in their first four games does not have to become the story of their whole season.

With Stoke, we got a win in our first home game - against Aston Villa - but that was our only victory in our first seven league matches after getting promoted.

The thing I remember most from that time is that Hull had come up with us and, after seven games, they had won at Newcastle, Arsenal and Tottenham and were in the top five in the table, while we were third or fourth from bottom.

I went out for dinner with my chairman, Peter Coates, and he said how Hull had made a wonderful start. I replied by telling him I bet you now that we finish above Hull... and we did.

The reason I thought that was because of the mindset of the team, and the fans.

I was confident my players were not going to go weak at the knees, and the togetherness we needed was already there in the squad, while the support was just off the scales, which helped us enormously at home.

Every defeat was taken on the chin, and accepted, but the lads were always ready to go, again and again.

It was Steve Coppell who said to me how you have to deal with the fact you are going to lose a lot of games - or at least not win a lot of them - when you take a team up into the Premier League.

It is a very unusual situation, to go from being in the Championship and winning regularly week after week, to dealing with defeat after defeat.

Steve told me to get ready for going on runs where we would not win for five or six games on the bounce, but then if we could win two or three games in the same period after that, we would fly up the table.

But getting your head around that is hard, and it is the same for the players who were part of that promotion - especially if you were dominant like Coventry were last season.

They were expected to challenge at the top of the Championship, but in my opinion over-achieved by finishing clear at the top.

It was different for Hull, who achieved a promotion under Sergej Jakirovic that no-one outside that club believed was possible.

They have started the season on fire, just like the Tigers did in 2008 when Phil Brown was in charge, and now they have to try to sustain it.

They are third at the moment but if they are 17th come the end of May, which is where they finished under Brownie, then that will be a successful season.

I will be taking a closer look at Hull's progress in this column in the weeks to come, as well as the other promoted team, Ipswich.

Gary O'Neil has a really tough gig at Portman Road but it is one he will relish. I gave Gary his senior debut with Portsmouth in the Championship in 1999 and he's a smart lad who was always football mad.

Ipswich are a great club and I hope both are successful this season. Gary has experience of the Premier League with Bournemouth and Wolves, and he is going to need it.

Including O'Neil, there are nine new managers starting with clubs in the Premier League. It's a bigger number than usual and I wanted to quickly run through all of them.

Enzo Maresca at Manchester City seemed like common sense to me, even before they started the season with four league wins out of four, because he has worked with Pep and the club before.

City had a large turnover of players with their ins and outs over the summer, but I'd expect them to be in the mix for all the trophies again this season.

Another place where lots of changes have taken place is Stamford Bridge. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has experience of playing in England and will understand that no game in the Premier League is a shoe-in - as Saturday's draw with Hull showed us again.

Andoni Iraola did an amazing job at Bournemouth but he will need all of his managerial ability and acumen to succeed at Liverpool.

At Liverpool, teams will drop deep and rely on counter-attacking situations. At Bournemouth that did not happen very often.

So, Andoni has to prepare his coaching philosophy to overcome teams who will definitely play deeper and be much more defensive-minded against Liverpool than they were against Bournemouth.

In my opinion, given time he will a great success but as he prepares to take his new team back to face his old one at Vitality Stadium on Sunday, we are already seeing that Liverpool will need more changes to develop into the title-winning side that their fantastic supporters demand.

At Nottingham Forest, Oliver Glasner did a wonderful job at Palace and I am sure we will see more of the same at the City Ground.

At the moment I know less about Marco Rose, Matthias Jaissle, and Pierre Sage, at Bournemouth, Newcastle and Crystal Palace.

Unlike the other managers I have mentioned, they have no experience of the Premier League but they are all joining established top-flight sides which is a huge help.

Finally, there is Alvaro Arbeloa at Fulham. He had a fantastic playing record at Real Madrid and Liverpool and coached in the Real Madrid academy and their B team before taking charge of the first team for the second half of last season.

While he has not had much experience in the dugout, he has worked with many top managers and players.

Fulham will be a real test for him, as we've seen from the way they have started the season, so again they are a club I will be keeping a close eye on - but there are plenty of those!

I got stuck into lots of topics in this column last season, at all levels of the game and covering every aspect of management, but I'd love to know what you would like me to talk about over the next few weeks.

Please make any suggestions in the comments section below - and also feel free to ask me any questions too.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

title: 'Mini Valverde' wanted by Chelsea - Garner is now Everton's main man
description: BBC Sport examines how James Garner has become Everton's most important player.
fullText:
Crunching tackles that help win hard-fought away points in an all-action performance are the kind of things Everton fans have become well accustomed to when watching James Garner.

Now the rest of the Premier League are starting to take proper notice.

Following Everton's goalless draw at Tottenham on Saturday, during which midfielder Garner bested a home line-up boasting the near-£200m midfield pairing of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, Match of the Day pundit Thomas Frank hailed Garner's display.

It featured crucial challenges on Tonali and Fernandes to halt promising home attacks - by a player who missed a significant part of pre-season after hernia surgery.

"Garner today was extremely good," said Frank. "He is aware; he's talking; he's organising.

"In a high-press situation, he does the recovery, and that's just so exceptional and so important when you are playing against a team who are dominating you.

"He was running so hard, so that's one side of his game, but also so important is his touches. He is a lot on the ball. It's through him that a lot of things are happening."

Fellow pundit and former Everton defender Ashley Williams said: "He's really impressive. If you're a centre-back behind him, he's the type of midfielder you want."

Garner was signed for an initial fee of only £9m from Manchester United in 2022, having spent the previous season on loan helping Nottingham Forest get promoted to the Premier League.

The academy graduate did not make a Premier League start for United.

After taking two seasons to settle at Everton under Frank Lampard and then Sean Dyche amid a backdrop of financial problems and points deductions, the 2025-26 campaign proved to be a watershed moment.

Garner played all but six minutes of Everton's Premier League campaign to spearhead a European push that lasted for much of the season.

In December Everton travelled to Forest with a depleted squad and won 2-0 to move within four points of the top four.

Garner scored Everton's opening goal in a commanding display that underlined his development.

Following that win, manager David Moyes said: "When I came in, I still saw a bit of a boy and I think I now see someone who's turning into a really good leader as well, beginning to take a bit more responsibility and grow up and begin to start to act like a real midfield player."

The data backs up Garner's growing maturity.

He ranked top for a host of metrics for Everton last season, in terms of creativity and physicality, making the most successful passes, tackles and interceptions, but also providing the most assists and engineering the most chances.

Perhaps most impressively, he stepped up in the absence of key winger Jack Grealish - four of Garner's seven assists came after Grealish's season was ended by injury in January.

"He's been fantastic since I came in," said Moyes. "I didn't realise probably how good he was. He's been so good."

Garner's consistent displays last season earned him a first England cap in a friendly against Uruguay in March.

He produced a man-of-the-match performance, topping the game for tackles and chances created.

After the match England manager Thomas Tuchel compared him with Uruguay and Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde.

"He's our mini Valverde," said Tuchel. "He played very, very good. I was quite sure that he will play good because he has this natural confidence and he's just very physical. He won a lot of balls."

Garner missed out on a place in England's World Cup squad, but those physical attributes could result in more caps in the near future.

He covered the most ground of any Premier League player last season - and 6km more than England midfielder Elliot Anderson - while also topping the overall rankings for tackles and interceptions.

Garner signed a new Everton deal in January, keeping him at the club until 2030, but that did not stop a £65m bid from Chelsea on deadline day this summer, which was rejected by Everton - an important decision given that Garner's versatility is likely to be crucial to a threadbare squad this season.

Everton can currently call on only 17 fit senior outfield players, with Christian Norgaard and Merlin Rohl sidelined because of injury, meaning gaps may have to be plugged throughout the campaign.

Garner has played at right-back and left-back for Everton in addition to his usual central midfield role.

He also played at right-back when England Under-21s won the European Championship three years ago, while Moyes has said he can operate as a number eight or six – a valuable commodity after losing 254 Premier League appearances in the guise of departed midfielder Idrissa Gueye this summer.

If Everton are to push back towards European football this season, Garner may well be their most important asset.

title: Released despite seven straight wins, baffled Mokaev vows UFC return
description: Muhammad Mokaev tells BBC Sport that he is still searching for answers about why he was cut by the UFC in 2024 and dreams of returning to the organisation.
fullText:
It has been more than two years since Muhammad Mokaev was released by the UFC - and yet he is still searching for answers.

In July 2024 the Russian-born Briton had just stretched his winning run in the promotion to seven fights with a unanimous decision victory over Manuel Kape at UFC 304.

From the outside, Mokaev appeared to have it all.

Victory over Kape in Manchester had seemingly further cemented his place as a top contender in the flyweight division and a title shot appeared to be within his grasp.

But later that night UFC president Dana White made the shock announcement they would not be re-signing Mokaev.

It was initially suggested Mokaev's behaviour in the build-up to facing Kape – which included clashes with his Portuguese rival at the fighter hotel and again at the weigh-ins – may have influenced the UFC's decision.

According to Mokaev, that is not true.

"If we talk about behaviour, right - if I'm a bad guy, why would you let me fight seven fights and renew my contract twice?" Mokaev told BBC Sport.

"If I'm a bad guy in the company and organisation, they would cut me after one or two fights."

The flyweight, who moved to Britain as a refugee when he was 12 years old, believes his wrestling-heavy style was a contributing factor.

Mokaev won his UFC debut via submission in just 58 seconds before beating Charles Johnson by unanimous decision in his second bout.

He says the UFC text his manager after that victory over Johnson saying "he needs to stop wrestling - we don't want these decision guy".

"I have around a 60% finish rate in the UFC. Four out of seven fights were finishes against top guys," Mokaev said.

"I don't know what else I need to do to show them - I was 21 when I was fighting these veterans and now I'm much better and much stronger.

"From 21 to 23, I beat all these guys. Even Manuel Kape, and he is ranked number two right now. I really don't understand the politics. I really don't know. I wish I knew the full story behind everything."

You only need one look at Mokaev's record since July 2024 to understand how determined he is to make his way back to the UFC.

Few fighters on the planet have been more active than the flyweight, who has competed eight times over the past two years.

Since leaving the promotion, he has finished opponents with chokes, body kicks, head kicks and punches, while also winning titles in BRAVE CF and ACBJJ.

Yet it has not been enough to catch the attention of UFC matchmakers Hunter Campbell, Mick Maynard and Sean Shelby.

Although Mokaev is in a WhatsApp group with Campbell and Shelby, he believes the UFC is constantly moving the goalposts.

"Hunter made me a promise. They basically wasted two years of my life," Mokaev explained. "That's how I feel right now. I don't think what they are doing is right."

Mokaev says he was also offered $10,000 (£7,399) to compete in UFC BJJ, a Brazilian jiu-jitsu competition, against bantamweight champion Mikey Musumeci.

Despite finding the proposed fee deeply insulting, he was willing to face the five-time world champion if the UFC offered him a contract afterwards.

"They said, 'no, this is different. BJJ is different. This is different. We have other plans.' I told them where to go," said Mokaev, who admitted his response to the UFC contained several expletives.

When Joshua Van defends his flyweight title in a rematch with Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331 in Los Angeles, California, on Saturday, there will be a sense of what might have been for Mokaev.

That is because Van, 24, became the first UFC champion born in the 2000s when he defeated Pantoja in December.

It was a feat that had long looked likely to be achieved by Mokaev after he signed with the UFC in 2021 and quickly soared through the ranks.

Only former UFC champions Demetrious Johnson (13) and Pantoja (eight) have recorded longer winning streaks in the flyweight division than Mokaev (seven).

It is why he remains steadfast in his belief that he is the best flyweight in the world and that he will one day have UFC gold around his waist, even if it comes later than he anticipated.

"The way I'm going to compete and keep winning, eventually they're going to send me there," Mokaev said.

"Back then I said, 'the best fight the best.' But it doesn't matter what happens with the situation, I think I'm the best flyweight in the world and I deserve to fight the best."

It is also part of the reason he has decided to sign one-fight deals rather than committing to longer-term contracts.

There have been more lucrative, multi-fight contracts offered to Mokaev since 2024, though he will only consider signing them if the UFC's stance on his return does not soften.

One of those offers came from the Professional Fighters League (PFL) to fight in its bantamweight division, as the promotion does not currently have a men's flyweight division.

Mokaev says he would be tempted to put pen to paper if the PFL created a 125-pound division following its merger with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions in July.

"I want to stay active because I'm still young. I just turned 26. Most people start their careers at this age," Mokaev said.

"I'm going to do what's best for my family."
